skills.name: Experiment 7: transformation of milk into yoghurt

note.text:
Aim: to make yoghurt from milk using lactic acid bacteria.
Materials: one litre of fresh milk (or powdered milk mixed with clean water), two spoons of plain yoghurt (the starter), a pot, a clean jar with a lid, a thermometer, a clean cloth.
Method:
1. Wash hands and all tools well.
2. Boil the milk to kill germs, then let it cool to about 40–45 °C (warm, not hot).
3. Stir in the starter yoghurt.
4. Pour into the jar, close it and wrap it in a cloth to keep it warm.
5. Leave for 6–8 hours, then keep it cool.
Results: the milk thickens and tastes sour.
Conclusion: lactic acid bacteria change the milk sugar (lactose) into lactic acid, which thickens the milk.

worked_example.problem: Why is the starter not added while the milk is still {t}?
steps: Very hot milk would kill them, so no yoghurt would form.
worked_example.answer: The heat would kill the bacteria in the starter.

questions.prompt: Which step or result is wrong?

right.text: Add the starter when the milk is warm.
Keep the jar warm for some hours.
The milk becomes thick and sour.

wrong.text: Add the starter to boiling milk.
wrong.explain: Boiling milk kills the bacteria: cool it first.

wrong.text: Put the jar straight into the fridge after adding the starter.
wrong.explain: The bacteria need warmth for some hours first.

wrong.text: Use dirty tools; the boiling will kill the germs later.
wrong.explain: Tools must be clean: germs could enter after boiling.
